title: Judge Blocks Key Parts of Trump’s 2025 Election Order, Including Proof-of-Citizenship Rule
description_medium: On March 25, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an election executive order directing the Election Assistance Commission to require documentary proof of citizenship on the federal voter-registration form and seeking to limit the counting of mail ballots received after Election Day. In June 2026, a federal judge permanently barred implementation of most of the order.
description_long: President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14248, “Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections,” on March 25, 2025. Among other provisions, it directed the Election Assistance Commission to add documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to the federal voter-registration form and sought to condition federal election funds on states following the administration’s rules. It also attempted to require that mail ballots be received by Election Day. States and voting-rights groups challenged the order, arguing that the president lacked authority to change election procedures that Congress and states govern. On June 24, 2026, a federal judge permanently barred the administration from implementing most of the order, including the citizenship-document requirement. The White House said it would continue defending the order. The case centered on federal authority over registration forms and ballot-receipt deadlines, including Congress’s power under Article I to regulate federal elections. The ruling left those requirements subject to the existing statutory framework while the White House pursued its appeal.

corrected_wording.original_claim: Original title adds a machine-decertification directive and DOGE access to voter files to the proof-of-citizenship order.
corrected_wording.corrected_claim: EO 14248 sought to add documentary proof of citizenship to the federal registration form and was later blocked in substantial part by a federal judge.

source_access_notes: PBS NewsHour report describes the federal ruling against implementing the proof-of-citizenship requirement: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/federal-judge-bars-trump-from-implementing-proof-of-citizenship-requirement-to-vote.
rationale: Removed original-title criticism from reader prose and replaced it with the legal question the election-order litigation addressed.
